فَرْفَخٌ (S, A, L, K) and ↓ فَرْفَخَةٌ , (L,) [the former app. a coll. gen. n., and the latter the n. un., Purslane, or garden purslane;] the herb called البَقْلَةُ الحَمْقَآءُ, (S, A, L,) which does not grow in Nejd, (L,) also called فَرْفِينٌ, (S, A,) i. q. رِجْلَةٌ: (S, L, K:) an arabicized word, from the Pers. پَرْپَهْن, which signifies “ broad-winged. ” (AHn, L, K.) ―
-b2- Also, the former, The كَعَابِر [which are things that are taken forth, or picked out, and thrown away, in the clearing] of wheat. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
